sections.heading: Lore
sections.text:
"This world has so many mysteries to uncover. We should get to know it better just like ... like how we should learn more about ourselves. Don't you agree, Professor?"
 Ardelia is a Rhodes Island operator assigned to Endfield Industries where she serves as an expert geologist under the framework agreement between the two companies.
 Ardelia's early work centered on volcanoes, but today her research extends into Ætherside and geological disasters. She spends most of her time in the field, venturing alone into disaster sites to collect samples, analyze structures, and develop theories that have become the cornerstone of Endfield's Blight countermeasures.
 Always humble and polite, she carries an inner strength that never seems to run dry. To her, happiness is simple: climbing another mountain, walking another path, hearing the voices of the world, and uncovering the hidden wonders of this planet.
 And if you can become good friends with Ardelia, then Mr. Dolly is sure to like you too.

sections.heading: Kit Intro
sections.text:
Ardelia is a 6-star, Nature, Arts Unit support who specializes in applying long-lasting arts and Physical Susceptibility to targets by combining her combo and Battle Skills. This makes her a universal buffer, capable of being useful in almost any team you’re able to consistently activate her combo in. To activate said combo, she requires you land a Final Strike on a target with no Vulnerable or Arts Infliction stacks, which can either be trivial or quite tricky depending on your team. In teams where you consistently burn through your arts/Vulnerability stacks, Ardelia can easily slot in. However, in teams that have lingering stacks, she can end up locked out of her combo for extended periods of the fight, hurting or blocking her ability to do her job.
 Assuming you’re playing Ardelia in a team that works for her, she also brings other perks on top of her consistent debuffing. Examples are the ability to spawn healing sheep via her Battle Skill and Ultimate, which when collected, heal the controlled operator or the lowest percentage teammate, helping keep your team alive in tougher battles. Ardelia’s combo also forcibly applies Corrosion without the need to trigger it via an Arts Reaction. Usually, she consumes this herself in order to apply her debuffs with her Battle Skill, but in some teams, just applying it can be important for enabling combos like Laevatain’s.
 As long as your team doesn’t completely lock out Ardelia’s combo, and you have a small amount of SP to commit to her Battle Skill every so often, she’ll always be a solid choice for damage Amplification and survival, no matter the team.

sections.heading: Combo
sections.text:
Ardelia’s combo is the foundation of her buffing/debuffing ability, making it one of her most essential abilities. It requires the controlled operator to perform a Final Strike against an enemy with no Arts Infliction or Vulnerability stacks to trigger. This causes Ardelia to attach a bomb to the target enemy that explodes after a short duration, forcibly applying Corrosion to them and surrounding enemies for a short duration. This [Corrode] doesn’t require or consume any other Arts Inflictions when being applied and is primarily used as a resource to empower her Battle Skill. It still works the same as normal Corrode that scales with Arts Intensity if you want to use it for that reason as well.
 Tip: One of the main considerations when team building with Ardelia is whether your team is likely to have lingering Inflictions or Vulnerability stacks that aren’t routinely consumed. If so, Ardelia may end up locked out of her Combo Skill for extended periods of time, hurting her viability.

sections.heading: Battle Skill
sections.text:
Ardelia’s Battle Skill is the bread and butter of her damage Amplification. At a base, all it does is cause Ardelia to charge forward toward an enemy, hitting for Nature damage after a short delay. However, if the enemy has [Corrode] when her charge collides, she’ll instead consume the [Corrode] stack and apply a 30-second Arts and Physical Susceptibility to the target, boosting the damage of every major element in the game against them. This is a debuff you’ll definitely want to maintain the majority of the fight on high-priority targets. This debuff is one of the main reasons you consider bringing Ardelia to teams.
 Tip: Ardelia’s combo and Battle Skill both have very noticeable delays in connecting to the enemy. Don’t waste time waiting for them to complete; instead, fill the delay with other operators’ abilities.

sections.heading: Talents
sections.text:
Ardelia’s first talent, Friendly Presence, is one of the most important parts of her kit and the source of the majority of her healing capabilities. Unlocking it grants her Battle Skill and Ultimate, the ability to summon “shadows of Mr. Dolly” to the field for 10s. These shadows are collectables in the form of sheep that, when touched by the controlled operator, heal them for a flat amount plus a percentage of Ardelia’s Will stat. Only 10 shadows can exist at once.
 Ardelia’s Battle Skill scatters 3 shadows, while her Ultimate scatters a random but, in most cases, higher amount. Also, if the controlled operator is already at max HP, the healing is transferred to the lowest HP operator instead, allowing Ardelia to serve as a full team healer as well. Go sheep hunting if you’re running low on health!
 Note: Operators you aren’t controlling cannot collect shadows and will simply pass through them.
 Ardelia’s other talent, Mountainpeak Surfer, allows Ardelia to gain a free Battle Skill cast under certain conditions. After consuming [Corrosion] by using her Battle Skill normally, if another enemy nearby still has [Corrosion], Ardelia will retarget them and perform a follow-up Battle Skill in order to consume their Corrosion as well. This effect doesn’t consume SP but can only happen once per Battle Skill.

sections.heading: Ultimate
sections.text:
Ardelia’s Ultimate’s main function is to trigger her talent, Friendly Presence. It costs 90 energy to use, and causes Ardelia to channel an eruption for 3 seconds, which spews out copies of Mr. Dolly into the air, which deal damage and a small amount of Stagger to enemies they land on. Each has a 10% chance to be converted into Shadows of Mr. Dolly by Ardelia’s talent. The main purpose of using this Ultimate is either for keeping the team alive or triggering weapons that activate when using Ultimates. Outside that, the extra Stagger and damage can sometimes be helpful too.
 Note : Even if the Dollys from the eruption all luckily land on the same enemy in short succession, enemies can only take damage/Stagger from this ability once every 0.3 seconds, limiting it to 10 hits total.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.text:
Ardelia’s gameplay is very simple and revolves entirely around keeping her Susceptibility on your primary target in most cases. To do so:
 At the start of fights, start with a Final Strike before applying your Vulnerable/Inflictions to get Ardelia’s combo in rotation.

 During the fight, ensure you weave in Final Strikes at moments after you consume Vulnerable/Inflictions to not miss out on the window for activating Ardelia’s combo

 After Corrosion is applied, if Ardelia’s Susceptibility hasn’t been applied yet or has a low duration, apply/re-apply it through her Battle Skill.

 When Ardelia’s Ultimate is available, use it if you require healing. If you’re using a weapon that triggers off of Ultimate use, time it to take advantage of its bonuses. If neither of those applies, either save it or use it for its damage/Stagger.

 Collect Shadows of Mr. Wooly to heal your main operator and or team

 Dreams of the Starry Beach (P 0 )

 Ardelia's signature is definitely her best choice when supporting Arts teams. It has great passive stats for her and after she consumes Corrosion to apply her Susceptibility, she also applies an Arts Damage Taken debuff for a long duration, as well as massively increasing her ability to boost the team's Arts Damage. The one catch with this weapon is that it does nothing for Ardelia when she's supporting Physical teams.

 2

 Stanza of Memorials (P 5 )

 When playing Ardelia in Physical teams, Starry Beach cannot be used, so this weapon is the replacement. It has servicable stats for Ardelia, but more importantly, grants all non-Nature Operators a large attack boost for a long duration after she uses her Ultimate. This is still a decent boost to Ardelia's teamwide damage boosting capabilities, but it isn't quite as impactful as her Signature is for Arts teams.

sections.heading: Description
sections.text: Eternal Xiranite is the go-to 3P set for all supports capable of activating its team-wide buffing effect and who can also benefit from the large amounts of Ultimate Gain each of its pieces provides. Ardelia applies Susceptibility frequently via her battle skill, which can trigger the 3P bonus, granted not as frequently or consistently as some other characters, meaning maximum uptime might need to be helped along by another Operator on this set as well. The INT, WILL and Ultimate Gain heavy pieces are all exactly what she's looking for from her gear.

sections.heading: Potentials Review
sections.text:
P 1
 Dolly Paradise

 Increases the Susceptibility applied by Ardelia’s Battle Skill by a notable flat amount, boosting her supportive capabilities nicely. Ends up being a nice upgrade to any team she’s supporting, making it one of her most impactful potentials.

 P 2
 Game Rewards

 Significantly improves the healing from Ardelia’s talent, causing it to treat the lowest HP operator in addition to the controlled operator, but at 50% of the value. When things get tough, ends up being a 1.5 times healing increase.

 P 3
 Explosive Eruption

 Increase the channelling duration of Ardelia’s Ultimate by one second from 3 to 4, increasing the number of Dolly’s she summons, while also improving the hit count of the Ultimate. Also increases the total amount of Shadows of Mr. Dolly, the Ultimate summons, on average by 1.2 times, giving you more sheep to collect for healing.

 P 4
 Rock Blossom

 Reduces Ardelia’s Ultimate cost by -15%, taking it from 90 to 77, improving accessibility to sustain in fights while also boosting the potential of Ultimate triggering weapons.

 P 5
 Volcanic Steam

 Reduces the cooldown of Ardelia’s combo by 2 seconds, improves its damage (unique multiplier), and also extends its Corrosion duration by 4 seconds, taking it from 7 seconds to 11. The cooldown reduction of this potential is a nice bonus, which makes maintaining Ardelia’s Susceptibility easier, and which also boosts synergy with characters that make use of her Corrosion. The extra duration on Corrosion is very nice in encounters where you don’t find yourself consuming her Corrosion every combo, and leave it active some of the time. However, it won't be as powerful in shorter fights or fights with continually new enemies where you do.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Ardelia is a universal unit able to be played in almost any team, with the exception of teams that leave lingering Inflictions, which lock out the use of her Combo skill. Because of that, she can synergize with almost any team composition. Here's what she can do:
 She's able to permanently maintain both Arts and Physical Susceptibility on targets for generic team-wide damage increases that work in any team.
 Outstanding supportive weapon and set options for even more damage amplification, with options that work for both Physical and Arts.
 Forcibly applies Corrosion, which, when optimized around, can lower enemy resistances to all damage temporarily if Susceptibility doesn't need to be refreshed.
 Only requires 100 SP roughly every 30 seconds to function at maximum capacity.
 Strong enough sustain to single handedly keep the team alive through most endgame encounters as long as smart dodging is used.
 Physical

 Rossi Physical

 Ardelia has highly competitive buffs that work for both Physical and Arts DMG, with an emphasis on Arts DMG if her Signature is used, which aligns well with Rossi's damage distribution.

 Ardelia does have limited use cases outside of full energy starts, with steep SP costs and Combo Skill demanding no Vulnerability or Arts Inflictions on enemies, limiting team options and making for awkward looping rotations.

sections.heading: Extra things to look out for
sections.text:
Against weaker enemies and those who struggle with sequencing all four characters at once, investing the time into establishing Ardelia's combo skill at the start of your rotation may not be worth it. Instead you can skip it and go straight to your physical rotation,
 Also against weaker enemies that may die in a single Crush, you can cut Chen's Battle Skill from the rotation to reduce its total cost to 200 SP instead of 300, making it immediately usable at the start of combat.
 Lifeng's Battle Skill has a long animation. Make sure not to use Ardelia's Combo skill until it lands, otherwise you may accidently trigger Endmin's combo before Chen's, ruining the rotation.
 Once you're confident in the timings, you can begin Lifeng's Battle Skill halfway through your Main Field Character's Basic Attack animation so that it lands right after the Final Strike, which will trigger Ardelia and then Chen Combo in quick succession. Just be careful you don't have Lifeng's Battle Skill land before your Final Strike, otherwise Ardelia's Combo will be blocked.
 Sometime's you'll have multiple Ultimates available at the same time and will have to choose which to buff with Lifeng's Link here is the priority order: Lifeng → Endministrator = Chen Qianyu

sections.heading: Laevatain Ultimate Usage
sections.text:
How you play within Laevatain's Ultimate state is once again subject to how many enemies are present, what cooldowns you have available, your current SP, whether the enemy/enemies will survive until the Ult ends and how you're playing (are you using animation cancels?). Giving a generalist rotation that takes all this into account at every point of battle is hard, but in general, here is what to look out for:
 If possible, ensure Ardelia's Battle Skill Susceptibility is active on your main target before Ulting.
 Align Antals Ultimate alongside Laevatains to take advantage of its Amp during your highest burst window. If using Ardelia on Stanza line-up her Ultimate as well for the weapons buff effect.
 Ensure you don't overcap on SP during Ultimate, use Wulfgard Battle Skill to dump it and accumulate Heat Infliction, but always save at least 100 for Laevatain's own Battle Skill.
 When at 4 Melting Flame Use Laevtain's Ultimate Enhanced Battle Skill to deal damage. Laevatain's combo skill should also be used when available. Both of these abilities freeze the duration of Lae's ultimate when used, so wont waste any precious time.
 In AoE scenarios, you'll have much more Melting Flame to work with, so budget your SP around that and use Lae's Enhanced Battle Skill when available.
 As Laevtain's Ultimate is drawing to a close, you may consider saving 4 Melting Flame stacks to immediately execute an enhanced battle skill after it ends to recover over 100 energy instantly, although this will require a modified rotation afterwards. If the enemy is likely to die during or shortly after Ult burn all your stacks

sections.heading: Wulfgard Usage
sections.text:
Wulfgard has a few quirks in this team to be aware of, so you get the most out of him and don't waste SP unnecessarily.
 When using Wulf's Battle Skill, use it at a time when the enemy isn't suffering from Combustion, otherwise his Battle Skill will change to the Enhanced variants that consume Combustion and doesn't apply Heat Infliction, costing Lae a stack of Melting Flame.
 Use Wulfgard's Ultimate as an additional way to access Lae's Combo Skill whenever it's off cooldown. The energy from this ability is crucial, so if Ardelia's Combo and Lae's Enhanced Battle Skill aren't ready, use Wulf's Ultimate to solve the gap, just be careful of the point above.

sections.heading: Extra things to look out for
sections.text:
Laevatain features a number of animation cancels which can be particularly impactful during her Ultimate, allowing more abilities to be fit within its short duration. If you're able to pull these off, it can elevate her damage potential.
 Using Ultimate Gain on Laevatain through either the Tide Fall + Hot Work set-up or other sources allows her the energy leeway to execute a 2 Combo rotation instead of 3, shortening the time it takes to get to Ultimate noticeably. However, while this sounds good, it puts heavy pressure on having enough SP to generate the Melting Flame stacks you need while also applying both Antal and Ardelia's buffs.
 Both the Opening and Post Opening rotations can be optimized in multi-target scenarios where more Heat Infliction can be expected.

 Lore

 "This world has so many mysteries to uncover. We should get to know it better just like ... like how we should learn more about ourselves. Don't you agree, Professor?"
 Ardelia is a Rhodes Island operator assigned to Endfield Industries where she serves as an expert geologist under the framework agreement between the two companies.
 Ardelia's early work centered on volcanoes, but today her research extends into Ætherside and geological disasters. She spends most of her time in the field, venturing alone into disaster sites to collect samples, analyze structures, and develop theories that have become the cornerstone of Endfield's Blight countermeasures.
 Always humble and polite, she carries an inner strength that never seems to run dry. To her, happiness is simple: climbing another mountain, walking another path, hearing the voices of the world, and uncovering the hidden wonders of this planet.
 And if you can become good friends with Ardelia, then Mr. Dolly is sure to like you too.

 Review

 Kit Intro
 Ardelia is a 6-star, Nature, Arts Unit support who specializes in applying long-lasting arts and Physical Susceptibility to targets by combining her combo and Battle Skills. This makes her a universal buffer, capable of being useful in almost any team you’re able to consistently activate her combo in. To activate said combo, she requires you land a Final Strike on a target with no Vulnerable or Arts Infliction stacks, which can either be trivial or quite tricky depending on your team. In teams where you consistently burn through your arts/Vulnerability stacks, Ardelia can easily slot in. However, in teams that have lingering stacks, she can end up locked out of her combo for extended periods of the fight, hurting or blocking her ability to do her job.
 Assuming you’re playing Ardelia in a team that works for her, she also brings other perks on top of her consistent debuffing. Examples are the ability to spawn healing sheep via her Battle Skill and Ultimate, which when collected, heal the controlled operator or the lowest percentage teammate, helping keep your team alive in tougher battles. Ardelia’s combo also forcibly applies Corrosion without the need to trigger it via an Arts Reaction. Usually, she consumes this herself in order to apply her debuffs with her Battle Skill, but in some teams, just applying it can be important for enabling combos like Laevatain’s.
 As long as your team doesn’t completely lock out Ardelia’s combo, and you have a small amount of SP to commit to her Battle Skill every so often, she’ll always be a solid choice for damage Amplification and survival, no matter the team.
 Combo
 Ardelia’s combo is the foundation of her buffing/debuffing ability, making it one of her most essential abilities. It requires the controlled operator to perform a Final Strike against an enemy with no Arts Infliction or Vulnerability stacks to trigger. This causes Ardelia to attach a bomb to the target enemy that explodes after a short duration, forcibly applying Corrosion to them and surrounding enemies for a short duration. This [Corrode] doesn’t require or consume any other Arts Inflictions when being applied and is primarily used as a resource to empower her Battle Skill. It still works the same as normal Corrode that scales with Arts Intensity if you want to use it for that reason as well.
 Tip: One of the main considerations when team building with Ardelia is whether your team is likely to have lingering Inflictions or Vulnerability stacks that aren’t routinely consumed. If so, Ardelia may end up locked out of her Combo Skill for extended periods of time, hurting her viability.
 Battle Skill
 Ardelia’s Battle Skill is the bread and butter of her damage Amplification. At a base, all it does is cause Ardelia to charge forward toward an enemy, hitting for Nature damage after a short delay. However, if the enemy has [Corrode] when her charge collides, she’ll instead consume the [Corrode] stack and apply a 30-second Arts and Physical Susceptibility to the target, boosting the damage of every major element in the game against them. This is a debuff you’ll definitely want to maintain the majority of the fight on high-priority targets. This debuff is one of the main reasons you consider bringing Ardelia to teams.
 Tip: Ardelia’s combo and Battle Skill both have very noticeable delays in connecting to the enemy. Don’t waste time waiting for them to complete; instead, fill the delay with other operators’ abilities.
 Talents
 Ardelia’s first talent, Friendly Presence, is one of the most important parts of her kit and the source of the majority of her healing capabilities. Unlocking it grants her Battle Skill and Ultimate, the ability to summon “shadows of Mr. Dolly” to the field for 10s. These shadows are collectables in the form of sheep that, when touched by the controlled operator, heal them for a flat amount plus a percentage of Ardelia’s Will stat. Only 10 shadows can exist at once.
 Ardelia’s Battle Skill scatters 3 shadows, while her Ultimate scatters a random but, in most cases, higher amount. Also, if the controlled operator is already at max HP, the healing is transferred to the lowest HP operator instead, allowing Ardelia to serve as a full team healer as well. Go sheep hunting if you’re running low on health!
 Note: Operators you aren’t controlling cannot collect shadows and will simply pass through them.
 Ardelia’s other talent, Mountainpeak Surfer, allows Ardelia to gain a free Battle Skill cast under certain conditions. After consuming [Corrosion] by using her Battle Skill normally, if another enemy nearby still has [Corrosion], Ardelia will retarget them and perform a follow-up Battle Skill in order to consume their Corrosion as well. This effect doesn’t consume SP but can only happen once per Battle Skill.
 Ultimate
 Ardelia’s Ultimate’s main function is to trigger her talent, Friendly Presence. It costs 90 energy to use, and causes Ardelia to channel an eruption for 3 seconds, which spews out copies of Mr. Dolly into the air, which deal damage and a small amount of Stagger to enemies they land on. Each has a 10% chance to be converted into Shadows of Mr. Dolly by Ardelia’s talent. The main purpose of using this Ultimate is either for keeping the team alive or triggering weapons that activate when using Ultimates. Outside that, the extra Stagger and damage can sometimes be helpful too.
 Note : Even if the Dollys from the eruption all luckily land on the same enemy in short succession, enemies can only take damage/Stagger from this ability once every 0.3 seconds, limiting it to 10 hits total.
 Gameplay
 Ardelia’s gameplay is very simple and revolves entirely around keeping her Susceptibility on your primary target in most cases. To do so:
 At the start of fights, start with a Final Strike before applying your Vulnerable/Inflictions to get Ardelia’s combo in rotation.

 During the fight, ensure you weave in Final Strikes at moments after you consume Vulnerable/Inflictions to not miss out on the window for activating Ardelia’s combo

 After Corrosion is applied, if Ardelia’s Susceptibility hasn’t been applied yet or has a low duration, apply/re-apply it through her Battle Skill.

 When Ardelia’s Ultimate is available, use it if you require healing. If you’re using a weapon that triggers off of Ultimate use, time it to take advantage of its bonuses. If neither of those applies, either save it or use it for its damage/Stagger.

 Collect Shadows of Mr. Wooly to heal your main operator and or team

 Potentials Review

 P 1
 Dolly Paradise

 Increases the Susceptibility applied by Ardelia’s Battle Skill by a notable flat amount, boosting her supportive capabilities nicely. Ends up being a nice upgrade to any team she’s supporting, making it one of her most impactful potentials.

 P 2
 Game Rewards

 Significantly improves the healing from Ardelia’s talent, causing it to treat the lowest HP operator in addition to the controlled operator, but at 50% of the value. When things get tough, ends up being a 1.5 times healing increase.

 P 3
 Explosive Eruption

 Increase the channelling duration of Ardelia’s Ultimate by one second from 3 to 4, increasing the number of Dolly’s she summons, while also improving the hit count of the Ultimate. Also increases the total amount of Shadows of Mr. Dolly, the Ultimate summons, on average by 1.2 times, giving you more sheep to collect for healing.

 P 4
 Rock Blossom

 Reduces Ardelia’s Ultimate cost by -15%, taking it from 90 to 77, improving accessibility to sustain in fights while also boosting the potential of Ultimate triggering weapons.

 P 5
 Volcanic Steam

 Reduces the cooldown of Ardelia’s combo by 2 seconds, improves its damage (unique multiplier), and also extends its Corrosion duration by 4 seconds, taking it from 7 seconds to 11. The cooldown reduction of this potential is a nice bonus, which makes maintaining Ardelia’s Susceptibility easier, and which also boosts synergy with characters that make use of her Corrosion. The extra duration on Corrosion is very nice in encounters where you don’t find yourself consuming her Corrosion every combo, and leave it active some of the time. However, it won't be as powerful in shorter fights or fights with continually new enemies where you do.

 Teams and Synergies

 Synergies

 Ardelia is a universal unit able to be played in almost any team, with the exception of teams that leave lingering Inflictions, which lock out the use of her Combo skill. Because of that, she can synergize with almost any team composition. Here's what she can do:
 She's able to permanently maintain both Arts and Physical Susceptibility on targets for generic team-wide damage increases that work in any team.
 Outstanding supportive weapon and set options for even more damage amplification, with options that work for both Physical and Arts.
 Forcibly applies Corrosion, which, when optimized around, can lower enemy resistances to all damage temporarily if Susceptibility doesn't need to be refreshed.
 Only requires 100 SP roughly every 30 seconds to function at maximum capacity.
 Strong enough sustain to single handedly keep the team alive through most endgame encounters as long as smart dodging is used.
 Physical

 Rossi Physical

 Ardelia has highly competitive buffs that work for both Physical and Arts DMG, with an emphasis on Arts DMG if her Signature is used, which aligns well with Rossi's damage distribution.

 Ardelia does have limited use cases outside of full energy starts, with steep SP costs and Combo Skill demanding no Vulnerability or Arts Inflictions on enemies, limiting team options and making for awkward looping rotations.

 Against weaker enemies and those who struggle with sequencing all four characters at once, investing the time into establishing Ardelia's combo skill at the start of your rotation may not be worth it. Instead you can skip it and go straight to your physical rotation,

 Laevatain Ultimate Usage
 How you play within Laevatain's Ultimate state is once again subject to how many enemies are present, what cooldowns you have available, your current SP, whether the enemy/enemies will survive until the Ult ends and how you're playing (are you using animation cancels?). Giving a generalist rotation that takes all this into account at every point of battle is hard, but in general, here is what to look out for:
 If possible, ensure Ardelia's Battle Skill Susceptibility is active on your main target before Ulting.
 Align Antals Ultimate alongside Laevatains to take advantage of its Amp during your highest burst window. If using Ardelia on Stanza line-up her Ultimate as well for the weapons buff effect.
 Ensure you don't overcap on SP during Ultimate, use Wulfgard Battle Skill to dump it and accumulate Heat Infliction, but always save at least 100 for Laevatain's own Battle Skill.
 When at 4 Melting Flame Use Laevtain's Ultimate Enhanced Battle Skill to deal damage. Laevatain's combo skill should also be used when available. Both of these abilities freeze the duration of Lae's ultimate when used, so wont waste any precious time.
 In AoE scenarios, you'll have much more Melting Flame to work with, so budget your SP around that and use Lae's Enhanced Battle Skill when available.
 As Laevtain's Ultimate is drawing to a close, you may consider saving 4 Melting Flame stacks to immediately execute an enhanced battle skill after it ends to recover over 100 energy instantly, although this will require a modified rotation afterwards. If the enemy is likely to die during or shortly after Ult burn all your stacks
 Wulfgard Usage
 Wulfgard has a few quirks in this team to be aware of, so you get the most out of him and don't waste SP unnecessarily.
 When using Wulf's Battle Skill, use it at a time when the enemy isn't suffering from Combustion, otherwise his Battle Skill will change to the Enhanced variants that consume Combustion and doesn't apply Heat Infliction, costing Lae a stack of Melting Flame.
 Use Wulfgard's Ultimate as an additional way to access Lae's Combo Skill whenever it's off cooldown. The energy from this ability is crucial, so if Ardelia's Combo and Lae's Enhanced Battle Skill aren't ready, use Wulf's Ultimate to solve the gap, just be careful of the point above.
 Extra things to look out for
 Laevatain features a number of animation cancels which can be particularly impactful during her Ultimate, allowing more abilities to be fit within its short duration. If you're able to pull these off, it can elevate her damage potential.
 Using Ultimate Gain on Laevatain through either the Tide Fall + Hot Work set-up or other sources allows her the energy leeway to execute a 2 Combo rotation instead of 3, shortening the time it takes to get to Ultimate noticeably. However, while this sounds good, it puts heavy pressure on having enough SP to generate the Melting Flame stacks you need while also applying both Antal and Ardelia's buffs.
 Both the Opening and Post Opening rotations can be optimized in multi-target scenarios where more Heat Infliction can be expected.
